title: Operator access routines and evidence scratch
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to map operator access patterns across hosted / dedicated / private deployments, identify likely evidence sources, and frame questions for the next auditor dry run. Not finished — lots of unknowns flagged.

Context notes (high level):
- We run three customer-facing modes: Hosted API (Redwood-managed), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for a tenant), Private (customer VPC / on-prem). Controls must be scopal (who has access where).
- Key risk bucket: excessive operator access to customer data or keys; undetected privileged sessions; weak break-glass controls; unclear evidence trails across environments.

Immediate evidence map (what I think auditors will ask for):
1) Admin console sessions and SSO logs (Okta) – account-level change history. Evidence: Okta admin console export (CSV) + session event IDs. Probably stored 180 days.
2) Cloud console IAM changes (GCP/AWS) for Dedicated & Private infra. Evidence: cloud audit logs, IAM policy change entries, GCP activity logs / AWS CloudTrail snippets.
3) KMS/HSM usage for customer keys (Private) and our internal signing keys (Hosted) – key creation, rotation, access events. Evidence: KMS audit logs, HSM access records, KMS key policy snapshots.
4) Jump-host / bastion sessions to Dedicated clusters (SRE ops) – session recordings or SSH proxies. Evidence: bastion logs, recorded tty sessions, session start/stop, principal.
5) Application-level access to customer ops endpoints (model uploads, model pinning, rollback) – API audit logs, request IDs, and traces. Evidence: per-request trace with user token and route.
6) Database admin ops (e.g., metadata DB writes) – who performed schema or ad-hoc queries. Evidence: DB audit logs, migration PRs, runbook approvals.

Open questions / assumptions to validate with Brennan / Sanya: 
- How long do we retain Okta admin change exports and are they immutable? (assume 180d but need confirmation)
- For Dedicated clusters: do we persist full session recordings from bastion or only session metadata? Where are recordings stored (S3 bucket name)?
- Private deployments: is customer KMS fully isolated or can Redwood ops request temporary access via support workflow? Need exact steps and approvals.
- Does our per-request tracing include the mapping from frontend token to backend operator identity when an operator acts as support (impersonation)?

Quick control sketches (for mapping to SOC2 categories):
- CC1: Logical access provisioning: SSO group sync -> role mappings -> on-boarding checklist (owner: IAM). Evidence: onboarding ticket, group membership change logs.
- CC2: Least privilege: role definitions and enforced RBAC in console + deny lists for specific high-risk actions (e.g., key material export). Evidence: role policy snapshots + sample enforcement logs.
- CC3: Break-glass & emergency access: documented emergency request flow, approval chain, TTL for temporary elevation. Evidence: break-glass tickets, Slack #break-glass thread link, time-limited role grant records.
- CC4: Audit logging & retention: catalog of audit sources, retention durations, tamper-detection. Evidence: retention policy doc + S3 bucket lifecycle + digest checks.

Sampling plan ideas (to prepare evidence pack):
- Pick 3 hosted-customer tickets where ops intervened in last 90 days -> gather audit-trace, Okta session, support ticket notes.
- Pick 2 Dedicated clusters where SRE performed configuration changes -> bastion logs + deployment PR + change request.
- Pick 1 Private customer where key rotation happened or where Redwood assisted with KMS -> show approval + logs.

Notes on evidence packaging:
- Auditor wants chain-of-custody: link each artifact to a ticket/PR + timestamp + principal. My plan: create an evidence table (sheet) with columns: artifact_id, artifact_type, timestamp, principal, linked_ticket, short_description, checksum/path.
- Need to capture human approvals: Slack threads are messy; prefer to capture a permalink + screenshot + ticket reference.

Potential friction points to raise earlier:
- Some older bastion logs are on a cold storage bucket that is not indexed; extracting a full session recording takes 24-48h and may require infra ticket. Flag to infra team.
- For Private deployments, customers sometimes manage their own KMS; we need clear statement for auditors: "Redwood has zero access to customer key material" or document the support workflow that allows access and its approvals.
- Traces: some early-run traces only store request_id without operator identity; need crosswalk to correlate tokens/SSO session ids.

Draft script / narrative for auditors (short):
- "Operator access is mediated via company SSO (Okta). Role assignment maps to least-privilege console roles. All elevated actions require a support ticket with approval; temporary grants are time-limited. Actions are logged across Okta, Cloud Audit logs, and application-level traces; we collect artifacts and link them to tickets for chain-of-custody."

Action items / next steps (assign):
- Brennan: confirm bastion recording retention and S3 bucket names (due 2026-03-12).
- Sanya: run quick export of Okta admin events for last 6 months and drop CSV in evidence bucket, label: evidence/okta-admin-exports/ (due 2026-03-11).
- Me (Tess): draft the evidence-table template and PR to trust-docs repo. Start with 2 hosted and 1 dedicated sample.
- Ibrahim: check KMS/HSM event retention & whether KMS operations include caller identity in logs for private deployments (due 2026-03-15).

Loose thoughts / heuristics (brain dump):
- Auditors like reproducible queries: prepare a short set of cloud query strings (gcloud/az/aws) to pull audit events by requestId/principal. Put them in the evidence repo.
- Pre-scan for gaps: run an automated check for "operator identity missing" in traces for the last 30 days and list offending request IDs.
- If we cannot produce immutable evidence for some artifact (e.g., Slack thread only), accompany it with an attestation note from two approvers.

Links I should add to the formal evidence pack (placeholders):
- Trust docs folder (confluence): CONFLUENCE:RED-TRUST/Operator-Access-Evidence-PACK
- Evidence S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/trust-ops-2026 (need read path)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/142

Random micro-notes:
- For interviews: ask SRE lead about "why" we sometimes grant long-lived session keys to support scripts; try to reduce that window.
- Check whether auditlog ingestion pipeline preserves event ordering; auditors sometimes ask about log completeness checks.

End of scratchpad. Will turn into a small PR with evidence-table and sample artifacts once Brennan confirms bastion locations.

Unresolved / follow-ups to capture when we reconvene:
- Exact retention periods for Okta, CloudTrail, KMS logs (fill into table).
- Confirm which Private deployments have customer-managed KMS and prepare standard wording.
- Decide on canonical storage location and filename convention for evidence exports.

-- Tess
